After **Kxh5**, White can push **g7** but material is down (lost knight, gained only a pawn). However, in the other three king moves (Kg5, Kg4, Kh3), White cleanly wins the undefended bishop on f6 with the knight, gaining a full piece (bishop for nothing).

The key move is **Nxh5+**, which forces the Black king to move, and in all lines except Kxh5, White wins the bishop on f6. Even if Black plays Kxh5, White has g7 advancing.

**Best move: Nxh5+**

**Main line:** 1. Nxh5+ Kg5 (or Kg4, Kh3) 2. Nxf6 (winning the bishop)

**Motif:** fork (the knight on h5 gives check and attacks the bishop on f6)

**Coaching note:**

When your opponent's king moves away from defense, look for forcing checks that exploit undefended pieces. Nxh5+ forces the king to move and leaves the bishop on f6 hanging. In all but one response, you win the bishop outright—a huge material advantage. Always scan for checks that hit two targets at once.
